kjv: For there are three that bear record in heaven, the Father, the Word, and the Holy Ghost: and these three are one. And there are three that bear witness in earth
mine: For there are three that testify: the Spirit and the water and the blood
note: The "Johannine Comma" (5:7b–8a) appears in no Greek manuscript before the 14th century (and then only in a few late ones, some with the words added in the margin), in no early version, and in no Greek Father during the Trinitarian controversies; it arose in Latin commentary and entered the Vulgate tradition. Erasmus added it to his third edition (1522) after a recently copied Greek manuscript containing it (minuscule 61) was produced. It is the only explicit Trinitarian formula in the KJV NT and has no claim to be original. Spans 5:7–8. Context: the Spirit, water and blood only (high confidence). 5:6 has just named the Spirit, water and blood, and 5:8-9 continue that argument; the heavenly witnesses break it.
